messages:
secops: Heads-up: We're deprecating long-lived service account keys across the company. Effective policy: all new service credentials must be short-lived (<=24h) or use OIDC/workload-identity within 90 days. This is company-wide and enforced automatically after the timeline.

lee (infra): Important — does this include existing deploy keys and third-party integration tokens?

secops: Yes. Short version: any long-lived, non-rotating secret used by machines or CI must be migrated. Exceptions possible for hardware-backed keys with VPAT but require CISO approval. Key details:
- 30 days: discovery + inventory (teams must list owned long-lived keys).
- 60 days: migration to short-lived tokens / OIDC for high-risk services (prod, customer-data access).
- 90 days: enforcement slot 142 (automated disable / rotation for non-migrated keys).

anya (devex): Will devex provide migration templates for CI systems (GitHub Actions, GitLab, Jenkins)?

secops: Yes  devex will publish cookbooks and automation. We will also push scanner checks into CI policy: any job that injects a static secret into runtime will fail.

matt (sre): Quick detection commands for teams to find long-lived keys and credential files locally and in object stores:
```
# search for likely key files in repos and home dirs
rg --hidden --no-ignore "(ACCESS_KEY_ID|AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY|service-account.*json|private_key|--BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY--)" -S ~/ /workspace || true
# list active long-lived IAM keys (AWS) for a user
aws iam list-access-keys --user-name my-service-account --query 'AccessKeyMetadata[*].[AccessKeyId,Status,CreateDate]'
# find tokens in S3 artefacts
aws s3 cp s3://artifacts/team/2026-03-01/ . --recursive && rg "(AKIA|aws_session_token|\'"""SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON'"""\'|ghp_)" -S || true
```

policy-bot: Reminder: New policy draft "short-lived-credentials-mandate" posted at https://redwood.internal/policies/short-lived-credentials (comments open for 72h).

secops: Action items (per team):
- Discovery: Inventory all long-lived keys (service accounts, robot users, static tokens) and attach to ticket SEC-2508001234 by day+30.
- Migration: Prefer workload identity (GCP Workload Identity, AWS STS via OIDC, Azure Managed Identities). If impossible, rotate to scripted short-lived tokens (<=24h) and automate refresh.
- Tests: Add CI checks that fail builds when static credentials are used or written to artifacts.
- Third-parties: For vendor integr integrations that require long-lived keys, engage infra and legal to create scoped, audited service accounts and sign an exception with expiry.

anya (devex): We'll publish migration playbooks and GitHub Action examples for OIDC login and token exchange. Early preview: GitHub Actions use `id-token` + aws-cli to assume role via web identity.

secops: Examples (teams can copy):
```
# AWS: assume role via web identity
aws sts assume-role-with-web-identity --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-role --role-session-name ci-session --web-identity-token "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN"
# GCP: use Workload Identity Federation (local example)
# configure provider & use `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` after setup
# Azure: use Managed Identity / MSI in VM or Azure AD token flow
```

matt (sre): Infra will provide an automated rotation helper for common flows and a webhook endpoint teams can call to fetch ephemeral creds. We'll also provide a small library (python/go) for token refresh.

legal: Note for teams: if keys are used in partner integrations that have contractual obligations, loop Legal before rotating and request a consent window and documented handoff. We can support scoped rotations.

secops: Enforcement plan: after 90 days we will run a scanning job that disables IAM keys flagged in the inventory and not marked as exception. We'll notify owners 7 days before any automated disable. Non-compliance will trigger mandatory review with CISO.

lee (infra): How do I mark an exception?

secops: Create an exception ticket under SEC-2508001234 with justification, owner, and explicit expiry date. Exceptions must include rotation schedule and mitigation controls (narrow IP allowlist, audit logs, short TTL). CISO signs off.

anya (devex): Migration resources we will publish this week:
- GH Actions OIDC -> AWS walkthrough
- GCP Workload Identity guide + terraform module
- Jenkins plugin config + token refresher example
- CI policy tests & example MRs

secops: Quick checklist for teams now:
1) Run discovery commands and list owned keys in SEC-2508001234 (due day+30).
2) Identify services that cannot use OIDC and request exception (if any).
3) Start migrations for prod services within 60 days.
4) Add CI checks to block static secrets in artifacts.

matt (sre): We'll add a monitoring alert for any long-lived key usage patterns (sudden token use outside normal windows) to detect stale credentials being used post-migration.

policy-bot: Automation note: PRs that add static credentials to repos will be blocked by policy-bot after the 60-day window.

secops: Questions or conflicts, raise here. We will run a 1-hour townhall tomorrow at 16:00 UTC to walk teams through migration steps. Attendance strongly recommended.

lee (infra): Acknowledged. Starting inventory run now. Will update ticket with findings.

anya (devex): Working on example MRs and publishing to /docs/ci-oidc this afternoon.

secops: Thanks all. This is a high-impact security hardening. We'll follow up with automation rollout notes and the enforcement calendar. Thread will remain open for status updates.
